Camara — the rookie Perez hit in Las Vegas — is CONFIRMED at Haas for all of 2027.

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 8:00 AM ET

The FIA has handed Sergio Perez a five-place grid penalty for the Qatar Grand Prix, following its investigation into the Turn 14 collision with Haas rookie Rafael Camara during last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Stewards found Perez fully responsible for the incident. Perez's front-right tyre made contact with Camara's rear-left as the Red Bull driver attempted a pass approaching Turn 14. The stewards determined that Perez was not entitled to the racing line and placed the entire blame on him. His original 10-second time penalty was converted to a grid drop after Perez retired from the Las Vegas race.

Perez maintains he was alongside Camara entering the corner and that the Haas driver didn't see him — but the stewards disagreed. Meanwhile, Camara handled the incident with composure and impressed enough to earn confirmation of his Haas seat for both remaining 2026 races and a full-time drive in 2027.

It is a complicated situation for Perez at Red Bull. A grid drop in Qatar, combined with the growing speculation about his future at the team, adds pressure to what should be a straightforward run to the season's end.

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 10:00 AM ET

Formula 1's dominant team of 2026 is heading to Qatar with a point to prove. Mercedes endured their worst race of the season in Las Vegas — George Russell crashed into the barriers and limped home in ninth, while Kimi Antonelli misjudged energy deployment on the final lap and allowed Lando Norris to snatch second place away from him.

For Antonelli, the defeat stings but doesn't diminish a championship already secured. For Russell, however, the stakes are higher. He sits on 264 points — tied with Norris — and 37 behind Hamilton with just 50 points remaining in the season. Las Vegas was a setback he cannot repeat.

The team says Qatar suits their car's strengths and that they're confident a strong weekend is coming. Russell has gone on record saying he believes Mercedes has a genuine shot at the front in Qatar. Given the team's performance over the second half of the season, that optimism isn't without foundation — but Las Vegas proved that nothing is guaranteed.

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 12:00 PM ET

The 2026 Qatar Grand Prix weekend begins Thursday with practice, and for the first time since Kimi Antonelli clinched the Drivers' Championship, the focus shifts to the battle behind him.

Verstappen arrives with 304 points and a 37-point advantage over Lewis Hamilton for second place in the standings. With 50 points remaining across Qatar and Abu Dhabi, the math strongly favors Verstappen — Hamilton would need to outscore him by 37 or more points over two races to overtake him. That's possible, but it would require near-perfect results for Hamilton and significant misfortune for Verstappen.

The more urgent fight may be three places further down the standings. Russell and Norris are tied on 264 points — just three behind Hamilton. Either of them could leapfrog multiple positions in the final two rounds if results align.

One notable constraint on the Qatar race itself: Pirelli has set a 27-lap maximum per tyre set. With the race running 57 laps, every driver is committed to at least two pit stops — adding strategic variation that could shake up the final order.

Practice begins at Lusail on Thursday. The race is Sunday, November 29.

**Character count:** 261

Racing Bulls just locked in Lawson and Lindblad.

One seat remains. Haas has Camara. The second slot — likely Bearman — is the last mystery. #F1Fanrecap #F1

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 2:00 PM ET

The 2027 Formula 1 driver market is almost fully resolved. With Racing Bulls confirming Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad for next season, 21 of the 22 available seats are now filled — leaving just one position still to be announced.

The open berth is at Haas. Rafael Camara is confirmed for 2027, but his teammate slot remains unresolved. Ollie Bearman, who currently holds that seat, is widely regarded as the strong favorite to retain it. If Bearman is confirmed, the 2027 grid is complete.

The other conversation is at Cadillac. The American team's second seat appears to be the subject of ongoing discussions, with Colton Herta linked as a potential debut driver. That would be a significant moment for American motorsport — a US driver in a full-time F1 seat — and Cadillac has the narrative incentive to make it happen.

Elsewhere, Max Verstappen's extension with Red Bull until 2030 provides stability at the top. At the junior end of the grid, Isack Hadjar is confirmed at Racing Bulls as one of the more promising young talents on next year's grid.

stories.title: Antonelli at 402 Points — Mercedes' Historic 2026 Season in Review

x_posts.label: Post 5A
x_posts.text:
**Window:** 8:00 PM ET
**Character count:** 240

Kimi Antonelli. 402 championship points. 9 wins. 98-point lead.

Two races left and he's already one of the most dominant champions in recent F1 history.

What a season. #F1Fanrecap #KimiAntonelli

facebook.long_form:
**Window:** 8:00 PM ET

With two races still to run, it is worth pausing to consider what Kimi Antonelli has achieved in 2026. The 20-year-old holds 402 championship points, a 98-point lead, and nine race wins. Mercedes have secured both the Drivers' and Constructors' titles. By almost any measure, it has been a dominant season.

That does not mean it has been without challenge. The Las Vegas Grand Prix — Antonelli's most recent race — reminded everyone that the champion is still learning. A misjudgment in energy deployment cost him second place on the final lap, with Norris capitalizing to claim P2. Antonelli finished fourth. He was gracious about it afterward, acknowledging the mistake and treating it as a data point rather than a catastrophe.

Toto Wolff, for his part, has been characteristically optimistic about what comes next. A driver who can build a season like 2026 at age 20, Wolff has suggested, is only going to get better.

There are still points to score and records to extend. The final two races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi give Antonelli the chance to close 2026 on his terms — and to give rivals a preview of what 2027 might look like.
